title: Context and memory in an agent

items.stem: Your assistant program calls the model three times to answer one student's question, using the usual loop. At the third call, what does the model receive as input?

options.text: Only the newest tool result, since it remembers the earlier steps itself
The instructions, tools, question, and everything that happened in steps one and two
Only the question and the instructions, with tool results kept on the server
A summary of earlier steps that the model wrote on its own at step two

items.stem: A student chats with the assistant on Monday and says they prefer metric units. On Thursday they open a new chat. Your program only sends the new chat's messages to the model. What happens?

options.text: The assistant knows the preference, because the model keeps past chats
The assistant knows it only if Monday's chat was long enough to be stored
The assistant does not know it, unless your program saved and loaded it
The assistant guesses it correctly because most students prefer metric units

items.stem: A run makes two model calls. The fixed part of the input (instructions, tools and question) is 2,000 tokens. The first call outputs a 100-token tool request. The tool result is 3,000 tokens. The second call outputs a 200-token answer. Counting only input tokens, how many input tokens does the model read across the two calls in total? (The program re-sends everything each call, and the second input includes the first call's output.)
In one or two sentences: why is giving the assistant a model with a bigger context window not by itself a good reason to put every machine manual into every request?
Your assistant uses a memory tool that the model calls to read and write note files. Who actually carries out each file read or write: the model or your program? Answer in one sentence.
